module_title: Advanced Email Architecture, Search Operators, and Browser Engines
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical exams, this advanced module analyzes the strict anatomy of an email address, spam classification, advanced Google search operators, and the core 'Rendering Engines' that actually power popular web browsers.

core_concepts.title: Anatomy of an Email Address
core_concepts.description:
A valid email address strictly consists of two main parts separated by the @ (At) symbol.
- Example: rahul123@gmail.com
- Part 1 (rahul123): The 'Username', chosen by the user.
- Part 2 (gmail.com): The 'Domain Name', representing the server of the company hosting the email service.

core_concepts.title: Spam and Trash
core_concepts.description:
- Spam (Junk): Unsolicited, bulk, or malicious emails sent out by advertisers or hackers. Email providers automatically filter these out.
- Trash (Bin): When you 'Delete' an email, it is not permanently destroyed immediately. It moves to the Trash folder, where it usually remains recoverable for 30 days before being permanently wiped.

core_concepts.title: Browser Rendering Engines
core_concepts.description:
The hidden 'brain' behind a browser that translates raw HTML code into the beautiful graphics and text you see on the screen.
- Google Chrome: Uses the 'Blink' engine.
- Apple Safari: Uses the 'WebKit' engine.
- Mozilla Firefox: Uses the 'Gecko' engine.

core_concepts.title: Advanced Search Operators
core_concepts.description:
Specific symbols used in Google to narrow down search results:
- " " (Quotes): Forces Google to search for an 'Exact Match' of the phrase inside the quotes (e.g., 'SSC CGL 2024 Notification').
- filetype:: Restricts the search to a specific file extension (e.g., Computer Notes filetype:pdf).

important_entities.name: CAPTCHA
important_entities.significance: Full form: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart. It is a security challenge (usually distorted text or image selection) used by websites to block automated Spam Bots and prove the user is a real human.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic CGL Mains statement-based trap! The rule is absolute: A valid email address can NEVER, under any circumstances, contain a blank space.
Email addresses are strictly NOT case-sensitive. Typing Rahul@gmail.com and rahul@gmail.com will deliver the email to the exact same inbox. Capital letters make zero difference.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Username (Your Name) @ Domain Name (The Server's House Address). The @ acts as the bridge connecting the user to the server.

exam_strategy_tips: In Mains papers, 'Match the Following' questions pairing rendering engines to their browsers are highly common. Memorize Blink (Chrome), WebKit (Safari), and Gecko (Firefox) perfectly. Also, ensure you memorize the full form of CAPTCHA.
